NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VII: KNOWLEDGE, CONSENT AND SHARED WORK (LCG-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume III concepts (201-300): weather readers and navigators, seed keepers and terrace builders, permission and consent, who leads and who is heard, homes built by many hands, songs for the uncelebrated, and a village writing its own story.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: The musicians argue over a song honoring the people whose work nobody notices: let them make one song, or one verse for each.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) and (friend) want to write a song for the people nobody ever sings about: the ones who carry water, sweep the meeting hut, mend the fences and sit with the sick. But they disagree: (subject) wants slow and solemn, (friend) wants fast and silly. What should they do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: They argue for a week, and end up with a song that starts slow and solemn and suddenly turns fast and silly in the middle. It should not work. It does. The water carriers dance to it.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: They write a verse for each person, by name: the sweeper, the water carrier, the old man who mends the fences. Some of those people hear their names in a song for the first time in their lives. One of them has to leave the gathering for a while.
